candidate_windows.window_text:
RoBERTa-base (Liu et al., 2019) is a workhorse in many NLP applications that has a good performance/size tradeoff. The model has 125M parameters, follows BERT's (Devlin et al., 2019) learning regime with some optimizations and slightly out

performs BERT on a number of tasks. $^{5}$ We used the RoBERTa implementation based on PyTorch from the HuggingFace library. We used a batch size of 4 for small and medium datasets, a batch size of 32 for large datasets, and a learning rate of $5 \times 10^{-5}$ . We didn't use warmup for the learning rate when training on small datasets, and on the rest we used warmup for the first 100 steps. An early stop was used if there was no positive change over five evaluations steps on the development data. We used the Adam optimizer with a default weight decay of 0.01. Each model was trained for one epoch on the Nvidia Tesla V100 GPU. To ensure reproducibility of results, we used a fixed seed for the PyTorch, NumPy, and Python random number generators while training the models. Furthermore, we included a CUDA parameter that stipulated the use of deterministic algorithms. $^{6}$ Each model was trained with five different random seeds to obtain more accurate classification metrics (Dodge et al., 2020); we report median $F1$ scores. We also report results of smoothed multinomial NB classifiers. $^{7}$
